# EASA kit · 11 — Concepts side by side (generated by `easa_kit.py` from `02_EASA/outputs/day/result.json`)

RF = reduction of the per-flight probability of starting the take-off unlocked with no effective alert, relative to no system. *Pilot acts* = every true alert is acted on; *pilot matches* = the pilot acts as often as alerts have been right (probability matching, abstract-level evidence). Option effect factors are [Y] (`inputs.json` → `options`). D (two-stage restraint) changes severity, not probability, and is not in the table (doc 23 §3.3).

| Option | RF, pilot acts [K] | RF, pilot matches [K] | Mass | Power | Real-world approval (outside the task) | Cost class [Y] |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Seated switch only | 1.0× | 1.0× | < 0.1 kg [Y] | < 0.5 W [Y] | standard/minor | very low |
| Seated + rear bolt | 9.9× | 2.3× | ≈ 0.3 kg [Y] | < 1 W [Y] | minor | low |
| LOCK-SENSE (chosen) | 1 901× | 3.0× | 0.5–0.6 kg [D+Y] | < 2 W [D+Y] | minor (EASA or DOA) | low |
| Dual everything | 2 191× | 3.0× | ≈ 0.9 kg [Y] | < 3 W [Y] | minor | medium |
| B · LOCK-SENSE Plus | 16 808× | 2.9× | 0.9–1.1 kg [Y] | < 3 W [Y] | minor + software assurance | medium |
| C · Powered over-centre lock | 7 121× | 6.1× | 1.2–1.8 kg [Y] | 20–50 W for ~2 s [Y] | major (TC holder / STC) | high |

**Reading:** every alert-only option collapses to about 3× when pilots stop trusting it, however many sensors it has; the powered over-centre lock keeps about 6× because it removes hazards instead of warning about them. That is the ladder: A3 now, C next with the manufacturer (it changes the latch itself), B only once the nuisance budget R-3 is shown. The official task sets certification and cost aside, so the approval column is context, not a criterion. The throttle shaker and the ground-only take-off gate (kit `12`) are not in this table: they are not modelled yet. Figure K1.
